analyst.summary: Mankind Pharma had a strong FY26 on paper - revenue up 17% and profit up over 30% - powered by its domestic chronic-disease business and the newly integrated Bharat Serums & Vaccines unit. But a meaningful part of that profit jump came from a low tax rate that management says will rise sharply in FY27 (from ~15-16% to ~25-26%), plus some one-off items - so next year's profit growth could look much slower than this year's even if the underlying business keeps growing at a healthy pace. At roughly 55x trailing earnings, the stock is priced for more than that normalized growth path can obviously deliver. We are maintaining Hold: the business is sound and well-capitalized, but the valuation leaves little room for the tax-driven earnings air pocket we expect in FY27.
